title: High-Throughput Multi-Provider LLM Gateway with Semantic Prompt Caching, Automatic Failover & Token Rate Limiting
problem: Applications relying directly on single LLM provider APIs suffer catastrophic outages during vendor downtime, waste budget repeatedly recalculating identical prompt completions, and face uncoordinated quota exhaustion across distributed microservices. Building ad-hoc client-side retries leads to stampeding herds and unpredictable billing spikes. This project builds a production-grade multi-provider LLM gateway in Python and FastAPI. The gateway unifies access across heterogeneous providers with automatic fallback routing, reduces inference expenditures through semantic vector prompt caching in Redis, enforces token-bucket rate limits per tenant, and exports real-time spend telemetry.

use_cases.title: Multi-Tenant Enterprise AI API Cost Optimization
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise software platforms serving thousands of internal corporate users need centralized billing control and spend limits across engineering teams.
use_cases.second_sentence: The gateway intercepts all model completion requests, checks semantic caches to return instant cached responses for repetitive queries, and tracks usage per project.

use_cases.title: Zero-Downtime Provider Failover for Mission-Critical APIs
use_cases.first_sentence: Production SaaS products relying on LLM backends must maintain continuous uptime even when a primary commercial provider encounters service degradation.
use_cases.second_sentence: The gateway monitors provider response latency and HTTP error rates, automatically routing traffic to secondary providers or open-source fallback models within 450ms.

use_cases.title: Distributed Rate Limiting and Quota Enforcement
use_cases.first_sentence: Cloud services offering LLM features to tiered subscription customers need deterministic token-per-minute and request-per-minute enforcement.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system applies distributed token-bucket rate limiting in Redis, smoothly queuing requests and rejecting abusive bursts with standard HTTP 429 status codes.

hard_parts: Implementing semantic prompt caching using vector cosine similarity that reliably detects semantic matches without returning stale or irrelevant completions
Designing circuit-breaking failover policies that detect degraded upstream providers without causing cascading request timeouts
Executing atomic distributed token-bucket rate limiting in Redis under high-concurrency client request bursts
Normalizing disparate multi-vendor streaming response schemas into a unified server-sent events (SSE) protocol
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase separating provider adapters, semantic caching managers, rate limiting interceptors, and telemetry routers
High-throughput benchmark report measuring proxy latency overhead, cache hit response speed, and failover diversion timings
Anti-fake verification script issuing a novel prompt followed by a semantically equivalent variant, asserting sub-15ms cached return and zero provider token usage

architecture.data_flow: A client application dispatches a standard chat completion request to the FastAPI gateway; the rate limiter evaluates the tenant token budget in Redis, rejecting requests that exceed quotas; the semantic cache computes prompt embeddings and queries Redis; if a semantic match exceeding similarity threshold 0.92 exists, the cached completion returns immediately; on a cache miss, the failover router forwards the request to the primary provider; if the primary provider times out or returns HTTP 5xx, the circuit breaker triggers fallback routing to the secondary provider; the response streams back to the client while writing to the cache and telemetry logs.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Redis Lua scripts atomically decrementing tenant token allowances; circuit breakers opening after 3 consecutive provider failures.

riskiest_component.name: Semantic Cache False Positives Returning Irrelevant Completions
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce high cosine similarity threshold (>= 0.92) and combine vector similarity with exact system prompt matching.
riskiest_component.fallback: Exact SHA-256 prompt string hash matching mode bypassing vector similarity.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a multi-provider LLM gateway in Python/FastAPI with semantic prompt caching, automated failover, and Redis rate limiting.
worksheet.q2: Target users: backend platform engineers, AI infrastructure developers, and enterprise cloud architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: enterprise AI API cost optimization, zero-downtime provider failover, and multi-tenant rate limiting.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: semantic vector caching with cosine threshold calibration, circuit-breaking without stampedes, atomic Redis Lua token budgeting, and multi-vendor stream normalization.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 200 prompt payloads, vector similarity fixtures, mock provider servers, and k6 traffic scripts. Mock queries only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: in-memory dictionary cache.
